newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to end gas flaring in next 12 years.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to end gas flaring in next 12 years.

text.p: Oil companies operating in Nigeria will virtually stop all gas flaring by the year 2008, according to presentations at an oil and gas seminar on Monday.
The general manager for gas for The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria, Michael Watson said his company planned to eliminate gas flaring by that time.
"What we have decided to do is to have flares out inside the date set by the petroleum minister," Watson said.

His company, a joint venture between state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) and Royal Dutch/ Shell Group pumps about half Nigeria's total crude oil output of about two million barrels per day (bpd).
It burns off into the air 1,000 million cubic feet of gas each day in the extraction of crude oil.

A presentation by Jackson Gaius-Obaseki, managing director of Nigerian Gas Co (NGC) said Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited, an NNPC joint venture with Mobil Corp, would eliminate gas flaring by 1999 when it completes its three gas projects.
The military government last month said it intended to end gas flaring from oilfields by the year 2010.
Estimated proven gas reserves are put at 124.42 trillion cubic feet (TCF), but the average utilisation level is 25 percent.
Watson said Shell would not embark on new non-associated gas (NAG) projects until all flaring is stopped.
"After the flares are eliminated, development of non-associated gas can then be considered," Watson said.
"But sufficient commercial incentive is required for rapid development of the nation's gas resources".
The Mobil projects comprise the second phase of the Oso gas venture, Ekpe gas compression and Edop gas injection, all of which will utilise 963 million standard cubic feet per day of gas.

Shell, Agip SpA and Elf Aquitaine -- joint venture partners in the $4 billion Nigerian liquefied natural gas (LNG) project -- will also produce a total of 1.082 billion standard cubic feet per day of gas to feed the LNG plant now under construction.
Chevron Corp's joint venture in Nigeria, Chevron Nigeria Ltd, is executing a multi-million dollar gas project at Escravos due to come on stream in May 1997.
